name: Basil Allard
life: “I still remember the seat left for me when I returned a grade behind.” People around Maré Coffee know Basil by a small Sunday habit. Basil likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I remember exactly who sat beside me when I repeated a year. That chair is reserved.
appearance: Basil has two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Look for short copper curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a red windbreaker with a little coil of soft measuring tape. In conversation Basil holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Basil admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Basil learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
family: Ruth Sutton is Basil’s stepsibling. Basil leaves the first voice message. Ruth calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A scar at the salon*, Ruth says, “I loved the scar in the picture because my own hands look similar.”
connections: Molly Neal. The remembered seat and the skipping rope give the reunion two different ways of welcoming someone back. Also in the story is Teresa Lopez (schoolmate).
